title: Alex Hormozi on Diary of a CEO: Offers, leverage and skill stacking from $1,000 to $100M
summary: Hormozi recounts losing everything in 2016, then rebuilding by licensing his gym turnaround system. He explains how he thinks about offers, value, leverage, skill stacking and choosing where to apply a skill, plus the mindset (pain, input/output math) that keeps him going.

principles.text: Make an offer so good people feel stupid saying no; if not enough say yes, improve the offer.
principles.quote: I just have to make things that are so good that people will feel stupid saying no and if we can't get enough people to say yes we need to make the offer better

principles.text: Value = dream outcome x likelihood of achievement, divided by time delay and effort/sacrifice.
principles.quote: we boiled down value into four variables

principles.text: Repackage what you have for a narrow niche that values it most to raise prices.
principles.quote: we redid the entire business model around finding only that Niche

principles.text: Leverage is output over input; stack labor, media, capital and technology to get more for each step.
principles.quote: leverage as the difference between what you put in and what you get out

principles.text: Sell the same skill to customers who value it most; bigger clients pay far more for identical work.
principles.quote: find the people who value what you have the most

principles.text: Stack complementary skills; each new skill makes the others more valuable.
principles.quote: every skill you add to your skill tool belt makes the rest of your skills more valuable
